# Tobit Chapter 3 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_003_page_001.jpg

---

**1** In my grief I wept and prayed, saying:

**2** "You are righteous, O Lord, and all your works are mercy and truth; you judge with true judgment forever.

**3** And now, O Lord, be mindful of me and look upon me; do not punish me for my sins and for the sins of my forefathers committed in ignorance before you.

**4** For they disobeyed your commandments, and you handed us over to plunder, captivity, and death, and made us a proverb of reproach among all the nations where we have been scattered.

**3** And now your many judgments are just, as you deal with me in accordance with my sins and those of my fathers — because we did not keep your commandments and did not walk before you in truth.

**6** So now deal with me as seems good to you: command that my spirit be taken up, so that I may be released and return to dust. For it is better for me to die than to live, since I have heard false reproaches, and great is the sorrow within me. Command, O Lord, that I be released from this distress; let me depart to the eternal place, and do not turn your face from me, O Lord. For it is better for me to die than to endure such great misery in my life and to hear such reproach."

**7** On that same day it happened to Sarah the daughter of Raguel, in Ecbatana of Media, that she too was reproached by one of her father's maidservants,

**8** because she had been given in marriage to seven husbands and the evil demon Asmodeus had killed each of them before they could be with her as husbands. The maidservant said to her: "It is you who kills your husbands! You have already been married to seven men and have not borne the name of any one of them.

**9** Why do you beat us? Because your husbands are dead? Then go and join them! Let there never be seen from you son or daughter to the end of the age!"

**10** She was deeply grieved by this, and wept. She went up to her father's upper room intending to hang herself. But she reconsidered and said to herself: "If I do this, they will reproach my father and say to him: 'You had one beloved daughter and she hanged herself because of her misery.' That will bring my father's old age down to Hades in sorrow. It is better for me not to hang myself, but to pray to the Lord that I may die and hear these reproaches no more in my life."

**11** At that hour she stretched out her hands toward the window and prayed: "Blessed are you, O Lord my God, and blessed is your holy and glorious name forever. Let all your works bless you forever.

**12** And now, O Lord, I turn my eyes and my face toward you.

**13** Speak the word that I may be released from the earth and hear reproach no more.

**14** You know, O Lord, that I am pure from every sin with a man,

**15** and that I have not defiled my own name or my father's name in the land of my captivity. I am my father's only child, and he has no other heir — no son, no close kinsman, no relative by marriage — for whom I should preserve myself as a wife. Seven husbands have died on my account; why then should I go on living? And if it is not your will to take me in death, O Lord, then look upon my reproach and have mercy on me."

**16** At that very hour the prayer of both of them was heard before the glory of the great God.

**17** And Raphael was sent to heal both of them: to remove the white films from the eyes of Tobit, so that he might see the light of God with his own eyes; and to give Sarah daughter of Raguel as a wife to Tobias son of Tobit, and to bind the evil demon Asmodeus. For it had fallen by lot to Tobias to inherit her before all the other men who had wished to marry her. At that very time, Tobit turned from the courtyard and went into his house, and Sarah daughter of Raguel came down from the upper room.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- Verse 2: Tobit's prayer opens with a formal doxological confession of divine righteousness before presenting his petition — a pattern common to biblical lament prayers (cf. Nehemiah 9, Daniel 9).
- Verse 3: "sins committed in ignorance" — the Greek agnoiai is rendered as a qualifier on "forefathers' sins" rather than a separate category; both readings are possible.
- Verse 6: The double "it is better for me to die" is preserved; the repetition in the prayer is deliberate intensification (cf. Sarah's parallel prayer, vv. 13-15).
- Verse 8: Asmodeus — LOGOS preserves the transliterated name without alteration. The demon's name appears nowhere else in the deuterocanon; it is a deliberate Iranizing element.
- Verse 10: The upper room (hyperōon) in ancient houses was associated with prayer, lamentation, and withdrawal from public life. Sarah's going up to hang herself — and then choosing prayer instead — is a spatial inversion of despair into hope.
- Verse 15: "only child" (monogenēs) — LOGOS renders with the most natural English term; "only-begotten" belongs to theological usage specific to the NT.
- Verse 16: "before the glory of the great God" — GII unique formulation, expanded from the shorter GI reading "before God."
- Verse 17: The lot-casting (eklērothe) refers to divine Providence arranging the marriage through heavenly assignment, not human random selection.

*— LOGOS*
